title: Impulse buying
scenario: Bilal sees a 40% off sale on headphones during a study break and buys them in two minutes. Later that week he is short on bus fare.
cost: $45 spent that was meant for transport.
fix: Use the 48-hour rule for anything that is not a need. Remove saved cards from shopping apps so every purchase takes a few extra steps.

title: Ignoring small expenses
scenario: Sara buys a $4 snack or coffee every day between classes and never writes it down. At month end she cannot explain where $120 went.
cost: About $120 a month, or $1,460 a year.
fix: Log every purchase for one month in the Expense Planner. Set a weekly snack limit and carry a water bottle and snacks from home.

title: Late payments
scenario: Hamza forgets his hostel fee due date during exams and pays a week late, which adds a late fee.
cost: A $15 late fee for something he had the money for.
fix: Put every due date in your phone calendar with a reminder three days before. Pay fixed bills the day your allowance arrives.

title: Unused subscriptions
scenario: Zara pays for three streaming apps and a gaming pass, but only uses one app regularly.
cost: $25 a month on services she barely opens.
fix: List every subscription once a month. Keep one, cancel the rest, and rotate if you want a different show later.

title: Spending without a plan
scenario: Omar spends freely in the first two weeks after his allowance arrives, then borrows from friends for the rest of the month.
cost: Money stress, borrowed cash to repay and no savings.
fix: Split your allowance on day one with the 50-30-20 calculator, then divide your wants money by four to get a weekly limit.

title: No emergency fund
scenario: Hina's phone screen cracks right before exams and she has nothing saved to fix it.
cost: An $80 repair paid for by cutting food money.
fix: Start a small emergency fund with even $5 to $10 a month. Keep it separate from your spending money.
